fixture_name: Six HAWK pedestrian crossings — US final design (FHWA case study, PD)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: Nighttime conspicuity of the HAWK display driving stop-decision reliability is a genuine final-design-stage safety issue with direct pedestrian-exposure consequences on an arterial crossing.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Pivotal claim (driver confusion from competing night-time background elements) is supported by a verbatim quote in EV-US-001 tied to the recorded case-study site issue; the inference link to pedestrian risk is transparently labelled.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly framed purely as a safety_concern under FHWA RSA semantics with no conflation into a compliance assertion; road-user scope and stage fit the us-fhwa:final-design context.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Names a specific, viable, FHWA-consistent treatment (retroreflective border/backplating) at the exact crossing; could note alternative measures against background clutter but remains actionable.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians explicitly identified as the exposed users if drivers detect/misread the display late, pairing beacon conspicuity with their protection.

justifications.substance: Pedestrian clearance adequacy for slower walkers at HAWK/PHB crossings on high-collision-frequency corridor sites is a substantive final-design-stage VRU safety matter under FHWA guidance.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Pivotal claim (clearance may be short for elderly pedestrians) is backed by a verbatim quoted passage in EV-US-016 attributed to the recorded case-study issue for these exact sites; nothing invented.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly framed as a safety_concern seeking verification of timing assumptions, kept categorically distinct from any MUTCD compliance assertion, consistent with FHWA RSA semantics.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Reprogramming clearance intervals at all six named HAWK crossings using a reduced assumed walking speed is specific, actionable, and viable at final design stage.
justifications.vru_coverage: Explicitly centered on vulnerable road users—pedestrians and specifically elderly pedestrians—whose exposure when conflicting releases begin is directly considered.
